problem: Given $P(A)=\frac{1}{4},$ $P(B)=\frac{3}{10},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{19}{40},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.

choices.value: $A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\cdot P(B)<P(A\cup B)$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\cdot P(B)\ne P(A\cup B)$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A\cap B)\ne 0$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\ne P(B)$
$A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, since $P(A\cap B)=0$

feedback.problem: Given $P(A)=\frac{3}{8},$ $P(B)=\frac{1}{3},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{17}{24},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
feedback.worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B)=0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{17}{24} & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{3}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{17}{24} \\  & =\frac{9+8-17}{24} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
